item.title: Baryon and lepton asymmetries across the cosmic QCD transition: effects of a 3D first-order surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.17401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the cosmological QCD phase transition by calculating the cosmic trajectories from the five equations that impose the conservation of the baryon and lepton asymmetries, the charge neutrality of the Universe, and $\beta$ equilibrium. We perform the calculation using for the first time the four-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q, \mu_S)$ Constant Entropy Contour equation of state, which for $\mu_S = 0$ ($\beta$-equilibrium) features a critical line and a first-order phase transition (FOPT) surface in the three-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q)$ space. We first show that, within the standard cosmological scenario with baryon asymmetry $b_{\text{obs}}=8.65\cdot 10^{-11}$, the lepton asymmetries alone can never induce a FOPT. We then explore the non-standard cosmological scenario with large values of $b$ and find that reaching a FOPT requires $b\gtrsim0.028$ during the QCD epoch. Such a value is compatible with observations only if the baryon asymmetry is diluted to $b_{\text{obs}}$ after the transition, which a period of little inflation would provide with $N\approx6.5$ $e$-folds of expansion. Finally, we study the phenomenological imprints on the equation of state and primordial black hole (PBH) formation, showing that pion condensation at large lepton asymmetries drives $c_s^2 > 1/3$ and shifts the PBH peak to sub-solar masses ($0.3-0.8\,M_\odot$), while the large-$b$ FOPT yields a narrow spike around $4.2\,M_\odot$.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Formaggio, Francesco Di Clemente, Tristan Gyure, Hitansh Shah, Roman Poberezhniuk, Alessandro Drago, Volodymyr Vovchenko, Claudia Ratti

item.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Lyman-$\alpha$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $\Omega_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $\sigma_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $\sigma_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.
item.dc:creator: Roger de Belsunce, James M. Sullivan, Mikhail M. Ivanov

item.title: Positivity Bounds, Negative Running, and the Weak Gravity Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.17408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study causality and unitarity constraints at one loop on a low-energy effective theory containing a photon, a massless scalar coupled to it through dilaton-like interactions, and a light neutral Dirac fermion with a Yukawa coupling to the scalar. In this setup, non-gravitational loop effects induced by the Yukawa interaction can drive the coefficient of the four-photon $(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})^2$ operator negative at low energies, apparently violating the tree-level positivity bound. Nevertheless, we find that these negative values are consistent with one-loop constraints from causality and unitarity, thanks to the low-energy contribution from the massless scalar to the relevant dispersion relation. We also examine the implications of this negative running for the Weak Gravity Conjecture in the magnetic limit of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes, since the RG-evolved Wilson coefficients can a priori shift the extremality condition towards the subextremal region. We find, however, that this shift is obstructed by the fermion mass induced by the same Yukawa coupling, which prevents the fermion from contributing to the running of the relevant operators down to the low-energy scales required to make the black holes subextremal. Finally, we discuss the relevance of negative running to loop-level positivity bounds in the SMEFT and to light-by-light scattering in the presence of a light scalar.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Fernandez

item.title: Analytic spread complexity in three-level systems and the spacing-ratio distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.17417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices. Here we consider three-level systems, the smallest setting with spacing correlations, and derive exact results for the spread complexity, the Krylov variance, and the Krylov entropy. At infinite temperature, the Krylov basis depends on the spectrum only through the ratio of consecutive level spacings, and the spectral variance enters only as an overall time scale. For Gaussian ensembles, these variables are statistically independent, and the averaged spread complexity and variance reduce to one-dimensional integrals over the spacing-ratio distribution encoding the level statistics. We establish universal late-time values of the complexity and variance, and an algebraic relaxation with exponents set by the Dyson index. We also outline the extension to $d$ levels, with the ensemble-averaged spread complexity expressed as a $(d-2)$-dimensional integral over the joint distribution of consecutive spacing ratios.
item.dc:creator: Pratik Nandy

item.title: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
item.description: arXiv:2611.17419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gr\"obner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.
item.dc:creator: Edward Hirst, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva

item.title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.17422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $\Delta \chi^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM at $4.1\sigma$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.
item.dc:creator: Georges Obied, Cumrun Vafa, David H. Wu

item.title: Invertible parafermionic topological phases in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.17429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Invertible topological phases of matter are described by gapped ground states of local Hamiltonians that are non-degenerate on any closed spatial manifold. Classification of invertible topological phases realized by bosonic or fermionic degrees of freedom is well-understood, particularly in low dimensions. In one-dimensional space, the classification can be understood through the boundary projective representations. We extend this paradigm to one-dimensional invertible topological phases of parafermionic degrees of freedom with symmetries. We define cohomological invariants that characterize distinct boundary projective representations and compute their stacking rules. Among other results, we show (i) how these cohomological invariants can be used to compute protected boundary degeneracy and (ii) how, in contrast to bosons or fermions, invertible phases of parafermions can form a non-Abelian group under stacking. For order-$N$ parafermions with $N$ a prime power, we define representative Hamiltonians realizing invertible topological phases with $\mathbb{Z}^{3}_{N}$ symmetry. We show that under stacking they generate a non-Abelian group of order $2N^3$. When $N$ is an odd prime, this group is $\mathrm{Heis}(\mathbb{Z}_N)\rtimes \mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2}$, where $\mathrm{Heis}(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ is the Heisenberg group of order $N^{3}$.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'{e} L. G. Mudry, \"Omer M. Aksoy

item.title: Geometric Bounds on Axion-Photon Couplings in Non-Supersymmetric Heterotic Compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2611.17467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the photon couplings of QCD axions and axion-like particles in non-supersymmetric heterotic string theory on Calabi-Yau threefolds with line bundles. After the St\"uckelberg mechanism and anomaly matching are taken into account, the QCD axion direction is determined by the QCD axion-coupling coefficients together with the axion kinetic matrix. We focus on the electromagnetic-to-color axion coupling ratio, $E/N$. When the physical electromagnetic and QCD axion-coupling vectors are proportional with the ratio fixed by the gauge levels, the QCD axion has $E/N=8/3$ for $k_3=k_2=1$ and $k_Y=5/3$, independently of the axion kinetic matrix. It is found that direct flux breaking of the visible $SO(16)_{\rm v}$ can produce independent QCD and electromagnetic axion-coupling vectors for the same level assignment. The Hermitian Yang-Mills equations and the heterotic Bianchi identity then restrict the departure from $8/3$. We derive analytic bounds for backgrounds with and without five-brane charge under assumptions about the axion kinetic terms and low-energy matching. An $SU(5)$-like model and a direct-flux Standard-Model-like model illustrate proportional and independent Green-Schwarz coupling vectors, respectively. For axions with no QCD coupling, we derive a geometric upper bound on their photon couplings and evaluate it in an explicit compactification.
item.dc:creator: Yuichi Koga, Hajime Otsuka

item.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern-Simons-Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf{8}_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf{8}_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's unitary symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. The continuum theories are proposed to recover lattice time reversal at criticality. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Guo

item.title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
item.description: arXiv:2611.17725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $\theta_i=\phi_i/f\in[0,\pi]$, conditioned on $\pi-\theta_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2\pi f)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_\phi\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $\Delta{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_\phi^2f^2=\Lambda_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $\Lambda_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Masroor C. Pookkillath, Gary Shiu, Shinji Tsujikawa

item.title: Classical weak antilocalization in electron hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak localization is strongly suppressed in electron hydrodynamics, where frequent electron--electron collisions rapidly dephase the Cooperon. Nevertheless, disorder can still produce a logarithmic correction to the bare hydrodynamic resistivity. We show that spatial fluctuations of the momentum-relaxation rate generate a classical memory kernel through the diffusive return of transverse momentum. In two dimensions, this return is logarithmic, as in weak localization, but involves a single shear propagator rather than quantum interference. Conservation laws and positivity of dissipation fix its antilocalizing sign: the return reduces momentum relaxation and hence the bulk resistivity. Unlike quantum weak localization, the logarithm is cut off by momentum relaxation and has a viscosity-dependent amplitude. For temperature-independent impurity friction, the resistivity correction scales as $-T^2\ln(T_\xi/T)$ in a Fermi liquid and $-T\ln(T_\xi/T)$ in a Planckian metal. In channels, the return competes with viscosity renormalization, and a width scan separates the two effects.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Cortijo

item.title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a M{\o}ller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.
item.dc:creator: Beatrice Costeri, Claudio Dappiaggi, Alberto Ferrari

item.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.17948v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.
item.dc:creator: Markus Fr\"ob, Albert Much

item.title: General $\delta N$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.17978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $\delta N$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Amin Nassiri-Rad, Hassan Firouzjahi

item.title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
item.description: arXiv:2611.18019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.
item.dc:creator: Akifumi Chitose, Hajime Fukuda, Kantaro Ohmori

item.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2611.18200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.
item.dc:creator: Finnian Gray, Hryhorii Ovcharenko

item.title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.18386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/\epsilon$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.
item.dc:creator: Shohini Bhattacharya, Alexander Sang Yi

item.title: Killing Spinors for Finite Temperature Euclidean Solutions at the BPS Bound
item.description: arXiv:2311.09427v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2308.00038], Anupam, Chowdhury, and Sen conjectured that the finite temperature Euclidean five-dimensional Cvetic-Youm solution saturating the BPS bound is supersymmetric. In this paper, we explicitly construct Killing spinors for this solution in five-dimensional minimal supergravity. We also expand on the previous discussions of Killing spinors for the finite temperature Euclidean Kerr-Newman solution saturating the BPS bound. For both these cases, we show that the total charge gets divided into two harmonic sources on three-dimensional flat base space.
item.dc:creator: Subramanya Hegde, Amitabh Virmani

item.title: Hadamard tails from flat space perturbation theory
item.description: arXiv:2510.25827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The short-distance singular structure of the two-point function of a free scalar field in curved spacetime has a universal behavior that characterizes well-behaved states (called Hadamard states). This includes a non-analytic term proportional to the Ricci scalar curvature known as the Hadamard tail. This is usually derived by solving a differential equation for the Green's function of a Klein-Gordon field in curved spacetime. We present an alternative derivation which leverages the equivalence principle and makes use of perturbative field theory methods. This allows for the computation of the short-distance singular behavior of correlators of QFTs in curved space. As examples, we apply these ideas to the two-point function of massless spin-1 and spin-2 fields in an arbitrary curved background, in general dimension. We also extend these results to the two-point correlators of scalar primary operators of an arbitrary Conformal Field Theory coupled to an arbitrary gravitational background.
item.dc:creator: Ameya Chavda, Alberto Nicolis, Alessandro Podo, John Staunton

item.title: Sparse Modular Forms, Lattices, and Codes
item.description: arXiv:2511.13816v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by sparseness conditions for holographic CFTs, we investigate sparseness of modular forms, lattices, and codes. For this we investigate the free energy of such objects as their weight, dimension or size goes to infinity. We construct families of modular forms that are sparse, such as the Eisenstein series $E_{2k}(\tau)$. We then investigate lattices that come from codes and introduce a sparseness condition for such lattices. We investigate the limit of lattices constructed from self-dual Reed-Muller codes and prove that they are sparse in this sense.
item.dc:creator: Christoph A. Keller, Ashley Winter Roberts

item.title: BFKL as a matrix: anomalous dimensions and running-coupling
item.description: arXiv:2512.07794v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The BFKL equation resums high-energy logarithms in a scattering process. We average over the angle between transverse momenta and replace the squared transverse momentum (virtuality) by $D$ discrete cells. The evolution equation becomes a real symmetric $D \times D$ matrix $H_D$. Its off-diagonal entries describe real gluon emissions that move the scale from one cell to another. Its diagonal is the virtual correction that makes those emissions finite. Powers of the matrix build up ordered emission histories, the inverse matrix propagates the amplitude between scales, and the eigenvalues and eigenvectors give the positions and the strengths of the singularities that control growth with rapidity. A row far from both ends of the matrix reproduces the BFKL eigenvalue. Some regions bring corrections to this for a finite Hamiltonian. These are the missing regions below the first cell and above the last cell, and the cell width. Matching the two scale powers allowed by a row yields the anomalous dimension. The matrix reproduces the leading-logarithmic small-$x$ coefficients. At fixed coupling, every finite matrix has only isolated poles. We show that they become increasingly dense as the logarithmic virtuality range grows, with a condition on their residues needed for the sum to approach the continuous BFKL Regge cut. Multiplying each real emission by a Bessel factor, which sums the leading double logarithms of the scale ratio, provides a test of how the fixed-coupling spectrum and its leading eigenvectors respond when long jumps in scale are suppressed. Finally, we place a running coupling which avoids the Landau pole. The number of positive low-scale states grows linearly with the logarithmic length, with a slope fixed by the kernel. A one-loop coupling with Landau pole, combined with a lower wall, creates an ultraviolet turning point and an Airy decay region.
item.dc:creator: Josep Rub\'i Bort (Instituto de F\'isica Te\'orica UAM-CSIC, Nicol\'as Cabrera 15, E-28049 Madrid, Spain), Agust\'in Sabio Vera (Instituto de F\'isica Te\'orica UAM-CSIC, Nicol\'as Cabrera 15, E-28049 Madrid, Spain, Theoretical Physics Department, Universidad Aut\'onoma de Madrid, E-28049 Madrid, Spain), Eduardo Serna Campillo (Theoretical Physics Department, Universidad Aut\'onoma de Madrid, E-28049 Madrid, Spain)

item.title: Holographic metals at finite volume
item.description: arXiv:2602.10460v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct the electron star solution in asymptotically global AdS spacetime, and investigate its thermodynamic stability properties, both globally with respect to the Reissner-Nordstr\"om and thermal AdS spacetimes, and under local perturbations of the thermodynamic variables. The solution is sourced with a perfect fluid at finite temperature, which implies that the ``suspended electron cloud'' previously reported in the literature does not appear as an equilibrium phase. We interpret the resulting system as that of a holographic metal confined to a finite volume. The corresponding grand canonical phase diagram reveals a rich structure of transitions involving three dominant phases, which depend strongly on the fluid parameters characterizing the star. Finally, we identify a quantum critical point at finite chemical potential, around which these different phases are organized.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Acito, Nicolas Grandi

item.title: Perturbative Nicolai-Map Diagrammatics: Application to Poincar\'{e} Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2605.29990v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a perturbative, diagrammatic framework for constructing Nicolai maps and apply it to four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ Poincar\'e supergravity expanded around flat Minkowski space. It provides an alternative to the coupling-flow-operator construction, which faces several obstructions when extended to local supersymmetry. Expanding the bosonic effective action and the Nicolai map jointly in the gravitational coupling $\kappa$ and the loop-counting parameter $\hbar$, we derive the Nicolai-map defining conditions, i.e. the free-action and determinant-matching conditions, order by order. The diagrammatics enumerates all admissible local terms in the Nicolai-map ansatz from the effective-action diagrams and reduces the construction to a finite system of nonlinear polynomial equations. Carried through order $\kappa^{2}$, the resulting constraints are found to be independent of the detailed bosonic input and hierarchical, order-$\kappa^{2}$ consistency further restricting the order-$\kappa$ data. A consistent Nicolai-map construction for the Einstein--Hilbert graviton sector is found to require the Rarita--Schwinger gravitino already at this order: Einstein gravity admits a Nicolai map only through its $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric completion, Poincar\'e supergravity, supporting Nicolai's characterization of supersymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Ji-Seong Chae, Hun Jang, Junhyeok Lee

item.title: Underdetermination in the Quantum-Mechanical Bootstrap with Mixed Functional Operators
item.description: arXiv:2605.30536v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The bootstrap method for quantum mechanics is a powerful tool for computing the energy eigenvalues of a Hamiltonian. However, we point out that a conventional implementation employing the standard bootstrap matrix may be insufficient when the potential contains different types of functions, such as polynomial and exponential terms. In such cases, the standard constraints may not fully capture the relations between the corresponding operator sectors, and the method may fail to reproduce the correct spectrum. A similar problem may arise when evaluating expectation values of operators of different types. This issue can occur in a wide range of systems, including statistical models and matrix models. We propose three possible resolutions to this problem.
item.dc:creator: Takeshi Morita, Worapat Piensuk, Pushkar Soni

item.title: Holographic SU(3) color superconductivity from color-octet condensation in AdS$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2608.22013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a holographic model of $SU(3)$ color superconductivity in asymptotically AdS$_4$ in which scalar and vector color-octet condensates form at finite baryon chemical potential. At $\mu_b=0$, a channel scan within consistent truncations shows that the favored sector reproduces the known $SU(2)$ s+p competition. At finite $\mu_b$, the s-wave order generalizes to an $S_1+iS_2$ structure. In the probe limit, the $S_+$ critical temperature grows linearly with $\mu_b/\mu_3$, while the p-wave critical temperature is independent of $\mu_b$. Once backreaction is included, the p-wave critical temperature decreases with $\mu_b$ and the p-wave phase disappears beyond a critical value of $\mu_b$. At high $\mu_b$, the balanced $S_+$ phase (with $S_1=S_2$) is the dominant color-superconducting phase, while the $S_-$ condensate, which signals the imbalance between $S_1$ and $S_2$, appears only at low temperature and low baryon density. Our results provide a holographic laboratory for color-octet condensation and non-Abelian color dynamics in dense matter such as neutron-star interiors.
item.dc:creator: Xin Zhao, Zhang-Yu Nie, Ya-Peng Hu

item.title: Pseudo entropy from entanglement entropy
item.description: arXiv:2609.14305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pseudo entropy extends entanglement entropy from a single quantum state to a pair of nonorthogonal states and is generally complex. Taking advantage of Cauchy-Riemann equations, Kramers-Kronig relations, and analytic continuation in state parameters, we show how and to what extent real and imaginary parts of pseudo entropy can be derived from ordinary entanglement entropy. For families with holomorphic coefficients in finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the reduced transition matrix equals the ordinary reduced density matrix formula evaluated at complex parameters. Then a convergent Taylor series gives the real and imaginary parts of pseudo entropy from even and odd derivatives of entanglement entropy at the real midpoint. The matrix identity also gives formulae for excess pseudo entropy and Renyi entropies, and interpolation formulae for families with polynomial coefficients. We apply these results to boundary-state quenches and thermal states in conformal field theory, and to fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states and quenches. In conformal field theory, Kramers-Kronig relations give the first moment of the imaginary part in terms of the central charge and one-point functions for boundary states.
item.dc:creator: Abhigyan Saha, Piotr Su{\l}kowski, Tadashi Takayanagi

item.title: Defect conformal field theories with free-in-the-bulk fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14176v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study codimension-two conformal defects for massless fermions that are free in a four-dimensional bulk, but interact on a two-dimensional defect. The bulk Dirac equation strongly constrains defect conformal field theory data: it fixes the dimensions of operators in the bulk-defect operator product expansion and, for bulk-defect-defect three-point functions, enforces a double-twist relation when only one member of a shadow pair is allowed by unitarity. The lowest modes of monodromy defects provide an important exception, since both shadow partners can be unitary and their three-point functions are instead related by a shadow transform. We illustrate these structures with defect interactions, including an exactly tractable bilinear flow and Gross-Neveu-type quartic couplings. At a perturbative mixed fixed point, we find an explicit interacting example in which the double-twist condition is violated and the two shadow channels combine to give a regular bulk-defect-defect correlation function.
item.dc:creator: Christopher P. Herzog, Daniel Lloyd-Jones

item.title: Bondi Four-Momentum Balance in Quantum NSF Physical scattering amplitudes and a numerical energy-balance test
item.description: arXiv:2610.14484v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Bondi four-momentum flux-balance laws provide a test of gravitational scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes. Starting from the classical matching conditions at spatial infinity, we formulate their quantum counterpart in terms of asymptotic radiative observables and the null-surface formulation (NSF) scattering operator. A principal result is that the NSF scattering amplitudes already satisfy three of the four resulting conservation conditions: total spatial momentum is conserved without imposing momentum-conserving constraints in their dynamical construction. Energy conservation, by contrast, is not manifest in the NSF amplitudes and remains an open analytical question. As a limited consistency test of the latter question, we use the unitary approximation $S_1=\exp(i\delta T_1)$ in the connected $2\to2$ and $2\to3$ channels, without imposing an energy delta function. At fixed $E_{\max}=2024E_i$, reducing the infrared cutoff from $10^{-5}E_i$ to $10^{-8}E_i$ decreases the relative mean-energy residual by a factor of approximately $584$ and the conditional energy variance by a factor of approximately $756$. These finite-cutoff trends do not establish energy conservation for the complete NSF scattering operator; they motivate an analytical investigation of the remaining condition.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Kozameh, Gerardo DEpaola

item.title: TQFT gravity dual to the orbifold groupoid of Narain code CFTs over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.30525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a companion paper arXiv:2610.26610, we classified the Narain CFTs obtained by gluing copies of the $A_3$ root and weight lattices along their $\mathbb{Z}_4$ discriminant group; for two hyperbolic pairs, this gives 22 even self-dual codes forming seven inequivalent theories at $c=\bar{c}=6$. Here we develop their physical interpretation and connections to 3d topological field theory. All 22 codes are topological boundary conditions of a single abelian Chern-Simons theory, whose invertible symmetries, including fractional $B$-field shifts, organize them into three orbits: free, mixed and torsion. Boundaries in different orbits are related only by gauging. We determine all gaugings of order at most four between the seven theories, by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$, with explicit twisted partition functions, and follow their effect on the spectrum and current algebra. We classify the topological surface operators of the bulk theory and identify those implementing these gaugings. Codes of the same group type are related by an invertible bulk surface; for different group types, every relating surface is non-invertible, and we find the minimal quantum dimension of such a surface. We give the fusion rules of the condensation defects, and show that theories self-dual under gauging carry non-invertible duality defects. Finally, we apply the TQFT gravity sum over topologies at genus one. We give a direct proof of the handlebody sum for any number of hyperbolic pairs, and closed-form weights for the handlebody and torsion contributions. For two pairs, the handlebody sum is the uniform average over the free theories and the torsion topology contributes the torsion theory, together reproducing the uniform average over all gluing codes. For three or more pairs, the handlebody sum alone is not a positive combination of code boundary states.
item.dc:creator: Rajae Sammani, Abdellah Sebbar

item.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30915v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.
item.dc:creator: Heng-Yu Chen, Yasuaki Hikida, Yasutaka Koga

item.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlev\'e Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the first Painlev\'e equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_\pi\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-\pi}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8\pi/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2\pi/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlev\'e transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin

item.title: Generalised $\Omega$-backgrounds in twisted $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills
item.description: arXiv:2610.40465v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce rigid supergravity backgrounds for 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills which deform its topological twists and generalise the $\Omega$-deformation of $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theories. We derive the twisted supersymmetry variations of the $\mathcal{N}=4$ Weyl multiplet, and the $\mathcal{N}=4$ matter multiplet coupled to a rigid bosonic background, for each of the three inequivalent topological twists. Other, more exotic backgrounds are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Iris Marieni, Itamar Yaakov

item.title: Carrollian minimal massive gravity and the fate of third-way consistency
item.description: arXiv:2611.09209v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct the Carrollian limit of minimal massive gravity. The limit is singular for the algebra and regular for the Chern-Simons-like data. The one divergent bracket points along the null direction of the contracted bilinear form. The Lagrangian is therefore finite while the brackets are not. The contracted curvature still obeys a cubic closure condition, forced on shell rather than identically. The third-way coupling itself, however, is removable. For generic parameters an invertible redefinition of the auxiliary field and the boost connection takes it to Carrollian topologically massive gravity up to a boundary term. The same redefinition fails before the limit. We solve for an anti-de Sitter vacuum and a Carrollian black hole, whose rotation parameter leaves the frame and survives only in the boost connection. The degenerate vector flavor metric obstructs the standard charge formula, which we replace by a canonical one. The boundary charges, obtained in two independent ways, carry no trace of the deformation. A Dirac analysis gives nine first-class constraints and no local degrees of freedom on any background. The massive graviton is removed. The asymptotic symmetry algebra is bms_3, with central charges carried by the Einstein and Lorentz-Chern-Simons terms. The black hole has two sets of thermodynamic data, each with its own first law. One obeys the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, the other keeps the Chern-Simons entropy.
item.dc:creator: B\"u\c{s}ra Dedeo\u{g}lu, \"Ozg\"ur Sar{\i}o\u{g}lu, Utku Zorba

item.title: Perturbative and non-linear analyses of gravitational turbulence in spacetimes with stable light rings
item.description: arXiv:2502.18643v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Some black hole mimickers, as well as black strings and other higher-dimensional spacetimes, exhibit stable light rings-regions where light or high-frequency gravitational waves can be trapped. In these regions, linear perturbations decay slowly, raising the possibility of nonlinear instability mechanisms. In this work, we study the cubic nonlinear wave equation as a proxy for Einstein's equations, using a four-dimensional model geometry that allows stable trapping. By employing a perturbative approach, we show that the nonlinear wave equation on the sphere with dissipative terms captures several features of the full nonlinear problem. This framework allows us to confirm a previous conjecture: all higher-order energy norms grow for arbitrarily small initial fluctuation amplitudes. Additionally, we analyze the system's mode spectrum at late times, revealing an inertial range dominated by a direct energy cascade. These findings further support the notion that spacetimes with stable light rings develop weak, high-frequency radiation hair, which will not generically lead to instabilities.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Redondo-Yuste, Alejandro C\'ardenas-Avenda\~no

item.title: Two Higgs Doublet Model from Six-Dimensional Gauge Theory
item.description: arXiv:2603.05857v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) based on a six-dimensional $SU(4)$ gauge theory compactified on $T^2/Z_2$. The six-dimensional gauge symmetry ensures that the tree-level Higgs potential is CP conserving and $Z_2$ symmetric, while the Yukawa interactions of bulk fermions are naturally aligned, suppressing tree-level flavor-changing neutral currents. The $SU(4)$ charge embedding accommodates the quark electric charges, while the group-theoretical enhancement of the Yukawa coupling in the sixth-rank totally symmetric representation leads to the tree level relation $m_t\simeq 2m_W$. We show that electroweak symmetry breaking can be realized and the observed SM Higgs boson mass can be reproduced through appropriate choices of the brane-localized gauge kinetic term coefficient and the bulk matter content. We also obtain predictions for the masses of the additional Higgs bosons. Furthermore, we show that the torus geometry affects both the Higgs mass spectrum and the couplings of the CP-even Higgs bosons to electroweak gauge bosons. Finally, we identify parameter regions in which the additional Higgs mass spectra are consistent with the ATLAS and CMS measurements of the W-boson mass within the approximation based on the scalar-sector contribution to $\Delta \rho$.
item.dc:creator: Kento Akamatsu, Takuya Hirose, Nobuhito Maru, Akio Nago

item.title: Affine ANEC selects the closed FRW branch for geodesically complete cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2605.18965v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the affinely parameterized averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along radial null geodesics, we prove that, within the globally nondegenerate Friedmann--Robertson--Walker (FRW) class with $a(t)>0$ for all cosmic times, non-static flat models and all open models cannot be both null geodesically complete and ANEC-satisfying. Bounded oscillatory or cyclic flat/open models obey the same obstruction; in non-static periodic cases the negative affine-ANEC contribution accumulates over infinitely many cycles, giving $I_{\rm ANEC}=-\infty$. The sign obstruction is absent in closed $(k=+1)$ FRW geometry, where positive curvature can offset the negative expansion contribution to the affine ANEC, allowing nonsingular, geodesically complete cosmologies with ordinary NEC-respecting matter. We construct closed-FRW scalar-field models and contrast them with their flat realizations, which require NEC-violating support. We show that neglecting small positive curvature in a flat reconstruction of the expansion history can produce an apparent phantom equation of state, with a percent-level shift at $z=1$. Our main result is a curvature classification of ANEC-compatible eternal FRW cosmologies within this class: non-static flat and all open models are obstructed, while the closed branch admits explicit complete realizations, with global de Sitter as the vacuum representative.
item.dc:creator: Nathan L. Burwig, Damien A. Easson

item.title: Domain walls through different cosmologies
item.description: arXiv:2607.28214v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study properties of domain walls (DWs) arising in the model with a double well potential assuming different early universe cosmologies: from dust through stiff matter domination to the limit of effective Minkowski space. Using lattice simulations we demonstrate that evolution of DW networks exhibits an approximate universality with respect to the cosmological equation of state (EoS). Namely, the wall area inside a given large volume is mainly determined by the particle horizon, while details of cosmic expansion play a subdominant role. As it follows, particle horizon rather than the inverse Hubble rate is pivotal in DW evolution defining the network correlation length and hence its phenomenology, e.g., the characteristic wavelength of emitted gravitational waves (GWs). Formation of closed DWs is shown to be very sensitive to the cosmological EoS and hence violate the universality, but their contribution to the total network is too small to change the overall picture. The universality breaking is also observed in the spectral properties of GWs from annihilating (biased) DWs: i) the IR slope of the spectrum depends on the EoS parameter; ii) there is a plateau in the UV part of the spectrum, which gets more pronounced as one stiffens the EoS. However, the dependence on the EoS is rather weak in the near peak region, which is most relevant from the viewpoint of pulsar timing arrays and other searches for the stochastic GW background. For a selection of primordial cosmologies, we provide fitting formulae for the spectra near the peak.
item.dc:creator: I. Dankovsky, D. Gorbunov, S. Ramazanov, A. Vikman

item.title: Collective superintegrable systems from the Guillemin--Sternberg torus action
item.description: arXiv:2608.01878v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a novel approach to the superintegrability of collective Hamiltonians invariant under a Hamiltonian action of a compact connected semisimple Lie group, $G$, on a symplectic manifold, $M$. For this purpose, we consider $\mathfrak{H} := \mathcal{J}^*(C^\infty(\mathfrak{g}^*)^G)$ and the centralizer $\mathfrak{F}$ of $\mathfrak{H}$ with respect to the Poisson bracket on $C^\infty(M)$, where $\mathcal{J}: M \to \mathfrak{g}^*$ is the momentum map of the $G$-action. By exploiting a Hamiltonian torus action that goes back to Guillemin and Sternberg [GS,1983], we demonstrate that the functional dimensions of $\mathfrak{H}$ and $\mathfrak{F}$ satisfy the equality $\mathrm{ddim}(\mathfrak{H}) + \mathrm{ddim}(\mathfrak{F}) = \mathrm{dim}(M)$. Together with a non-triviality condition, this ensures that the Abelian Poisson algebra $\mathfrak{H}\subset C^\infty(M)$ represents a superintegrable system, and it also follows that the momentum map of the GS torus action yields action variables for the system. Our work provides new insight into collective superintegrability complementing earlier results of Bolsinov and Jovanovi\'{c}.
item.dc:creator: L. Feher

item.title: Living on the Edge of Effective Field Theory: Near-Extremal Black Holes in Quadratic Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.05268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Near-extremal black holes can amplify higher-derivative corrections to general relativity, making them sharp probes of the perturbative control of gravitational effective field theory. We study this question in quadratic gravity with a dynamical scalar degree of freedom, focusing on dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Using pseudospectral methods, we construct rapidly rotating exterior solutions at fixed surface gravity and fixed horizon angular velocity, and follow this controlled family toward extremality. In dynamical Chern-Simons gravity, the sequence approaches an asymptotically flat extremal exterior whose near-horizon limit agrees with the dynamical-Chern-Simons-deformed near-horizon extremal Kerr geometry and inherits its enhanced $SO(2,1)\times U(1)$ symmetry. In scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity, the same limiting procedure behaves differently: the scalar develops an unavoidable logarithmic singularity at the horizon, the exterior metric develops a small boundary layer near the horizon, and the scalar-Gauss-Bonnet-deformed near-horizon extremal solution is not connected to a regular asymptotically flat exterior. We then use curvature invariants and tidal forces to diagnose the breakdown of the perturbative effective-field-theory expansion. We find that scalar curvature invariants can remain finite at the horizon even when tidal forces measured by infalling observers diverge as inverse powers of the surface gravity. These results separate distinct notions of effective-field-theory breakdown near extremality and provide a perturbative validity estimate that can be compared with current bounds on the dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar-Gauss-Bonnet couplings.
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Ka-Ho Lam, Gary T. Horowitz, Nicol\'as Yunes

item.title: Multiparameter Quantum Affine Spaces and the Scalene Yang--Baxter Equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.20714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct representation-independent families of solutions of the non-braided scalene Yang--Baxter equation from quadratic noncommutative algebras. Beginning with two anticommuting generators, we obtain a continuous deformation in terms of quantum-plane algebras and extend the construction to an arbitrary number of generators. In the latter case the scalene Yang--Baxter relation fixes the multiparameter exchange matrix to an exact multiplicative form, thereby selecting a distinguished subclass of multiparameter quantum affine spaces. We construct finite-dimensional realizations using singular matrices and finite Heisenberg--Weyl operators, as well as infinite-dimensional realizations in terms of bilateral weighted shifts and multiplicative-shift operators. The explicit realizations are generically weakly purely scalene: their individual constituent operators do not satisfy the ordinary constant non-braided Yang--Baxter equation. For selected finite-dimensional realizations, we additionally establish strong purity by obstructing a generic common meromorphic Yang--Baxter parametrization, even up to consistent invertible local similarities and nonzero scalar rescalings. These results provide a representation-independent algebraic framework for constructing scalene triples and a starting point for investigating their possible applications to quantum integrability.
item.dc:creator: Pramod Padmanabhan, Somnath Maity, Vladimir Korepin

item.title: Inhomogeneous Cosmologies with Bumpy Structure from Superfluid Pionic Vortices and the propagation of electromagnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2608.24666v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we introduce exact cosmological solutions in General Relativity in (3+1) dimensions which take into account both the usual fluid component as well as a superfluid component describing superfluid Pionic vortices. Such superfluid vortices are source of inhomogeneities which can be treated exactly, no perturbation theory is required. These analytic solutions are relevant to obtain a non-perturbative description of inhomogeneities in cosmology. We discuss the peculiar effects of these hadronic inhomogeneities on the propagation of electromagnetic fields on such cosmological backgrounds analyzing possible observable effects. Finally, the properties that the effective superfluid satisfy for such solutions to exist are discussed, together with possible extensions of this family of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Canfora, Alex Giacomini, Nikolaos Dimakis, Andronikos Paliathanasis

item.title: Quasicrystalline Inflation: From the Cosmological Dipole to Primordial Diffraction
item.description: arXiv:2609.02142v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose quasicrystalline inflation. Six quasiperiodic phases decompose into three phonons and three phasons. It turns out that a coherent pure-phason displacement can generate a local power dipole while the linear traceless quadrupole vanishes. From spatially varying quadratic effective field theory, we derive off-diagonal correlations whose momentum transfer is restricted to integer combinations of the six icosahedral wavevectors. These correlated off-diagonal signals provide a characteristic observational signature of primordial quasiperiodic order, primordial diffraction.
item.dc:creator: Jiro Soda

item.title: Photon evolution through light-particle conversion in stochastic magnetic fields: Kramers--Kronig relations and universality
item.description: arXiv:2610.11346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study photon conversion into light particles, such as dilatons, axions, and gravitons, induced by background magnetic fields, and formulate the resulting evolution in terms of the Stokes parameters. We show that photon conversion reduces to an effective non-unitary evolution of the photon sector. In the perturbative regime, the Hermitian and anti-Hermitian parts of the effective photon Hamiltonian are related through Kramers--Kronig relations, revealing that the changes in the Stokes parameters are not independent. We apply this general framework to photon evolution in Gaussian stochastic magnetic fields with possible helicity, and derive the ensemble-averaged evolution of the Stokes parameters. We find that two nonzero contributions arise even in the absence of magnetic helicity, which respectively correspond to the overall attenuation of all the Stokes parameters and to an irrelevant overall phase. We also find that magnetic helicity gives rise to two additional contributions, one of which changes the circular polarization while the other induces a rotation of linear polarization. These contributions form two Kramers--Kronig pairs. In particular, photon conversion induced by magnetic helicity is accompanied by both circular-polarization and birefringent responses. The same structure appears in dilaton-photon, axion-photon, and graviton-photon systems, revealing universality of photon conversion in magnetic fields.
item.dc:creator: Wataru Chiba, Ryusuke Jinno, Kimihiro Nomura
